About Aethron

The Mac app for owning your website.

Aethron is built by Jomiez: five AI agents that migrate templates, rebuild screenshots, check every page, fix what breaks and port your site to any framework.

Our values

The values behind Aethron.

Four principles we wrote down early. They still decide what ships and what does not.

01

Owners first

Every feature has to leave you owning more of your site. If it ties you to a platform, it does not ship.

03

Measure, don't guess

A change is kept only when Aethron has checked it. A model saying it is done is never proof.

Kept short on purpose

Four principles, written in 2026

02

Keep the design

A template's designer did the hard part. We change the words, images and links, and keep every animation they made.

04

Ship the site

A site you can publish today beats a perfect one next month. We release often and fix in public.

Our story

How Aethron came to be.

The releases and decisions that shaped Aethron, from one template to a Mac app.

Oct 2026

Updates itself

Aethron for Mac updates itself in place, and every push is checked before it ships.

Sep 2026

Screenshot to code

Drop a screenshot and Aethron writes a real, responsive page, measured against the picture.

Aug 2026

Port to Astro

Port turns a migrated site into Next.js, Astro, React or Vue, graded against the original.

Jul 2026

Any model

Aethron opens its tools to any AI agent over MCP. Another agent migrates a site on its own.

Jul 2026

The Mac app

Aethron becomes a Mac app: your templates and sites stay on your own computer.

Jul 2026

Map and Scan

The migration and checking agents learn Webflow as well as Framer.

Jul 2026

First migration

Our first real template becomes a site we own: 559 lines filled, every page verified.

Jul 2026

Jomiez starts Aethron

Jomiez starts building Aethron to own the templates it buys.

Jul 2026

One template, too many hours

Tim, Jomiez's CEO, buys a Framer template and spends a week making it his. Aethron starts there.

How we work

How we build each feature, from a broken template to a release.

Step

1

2

3

4

Step

01

Watch real migrations

Every feature starts with a template that fought back. We run real sites, note where they break, and write the fix down first.

Step

02

Build in the open

We share early builds with designers who migrate templates every week, long before anything is polished.

Step

03

Check everything

Every change runs through a build, a file check and a real browser before it reaches you.

Step

04

Fix in public

We release often and keep a written record of every bug and how it was fixed.
